component.vulnerableCodeAssessment: Exact Debian 1.3.1 source has no gz_vacate, but gz_write/gzputc/gzprintf/gzvprintf remain. Debian and Ubuntu leave the scope disputed because the reproducer also crashes older releases. This exact package therefore remains unresolved; absence of gz_vacate alone is not a NOT_AFFECTED basis.

findings.attackerControlledInput: Web request data and public provider responses are untrusted inputs. No application source path to node:zlib gzip or C gz* calls, and no subprocess invocation, was found. However, no claim is made that attacker-controlled input cannot reach every installed consumer or indirect dynamic lookup path.
exploitPrerequisites: CVE-described path: a non-blocking gzwrite stalls, followed by gzprintf/gzvprintf operating on stale input state in gz_vacate; this function is absent from Debian zlib 1.3.1 source.
Ubuntu records that its reproducer also crashes zlib 1.3.0/1.3.1; Debian security maintainer has not determined whether this older-version behavior is a separate issue or within the CVE assignment.

Exact-runtime exploitability would require an attacker-controlled route to an affected C gzip operation or equivalent path; no application call was observed, but indirect dlsym/API paths are not proven unreachable.
findings.reachability: System zlib is installed but is not mapped by the current web/worker Node processes. /usr/bin/dpkg-deb and libapt-pkg directly import gz APIs; libcrypto imports deflate/inflate. The Node executable has no DT_NEEDED libz, but its embedded zlib symbols include gz APIs and the executable imports dlsym. The loaded Next SWC addon contains no literal gz API names; literal scanning cannot exclude computed lookup. No direct app C gzip path was found. This runtime evidence does not settle the disputed CVE scope.
findings.networkExposure: Web is bound to 127.0.0.1:3000; worker has no published port. Public provider payloads and local HTTP request data remain untrusted input.
findings.privilegeContext: Current web and worker Node processes run UID/GID 1000 with CapEff=0. This narrows impact but does not prove the vulnerable behavior unreachable.
findings.mitigation: No scanner suppression. Current app source and process map show no direct system-libz gzip path; Node uses its bundled streaming deflate/inflate binding. Exact installed system libz still exports related gz APIs, and other installed consumers/indirect symbol paths remain relevant. Runtime controls are supporting evidence only.

vex.rationale: The earlier NOT_AFFECTED proposal is withdrawn. The exact 1.3.1 source lacks gz_vacate, but Debian declined to mark this release not affected pending upstream scope and Ubuntu reports older-version reproducer behavior. Exact-runtime evidence narrows direct reachability but does not resolve CVE assignment scope or all indirect paths. No disposition is proposed.
